claims.claim: It was a very dry year. Winter and spring rain was about 10 inches, less than a third of the usual.
claims.note: One source for the figure. Harvest Napa agrees the season was dry after January and February rain. Search summaries call it the second year of a severe drought.

claims.claim: Budbreak was in April. Wine Independent says a cool February and March kept Cabernet dormant until mid-April.
claims.note: Some reports describe an early spring. See conflicts.

claims.claim: Yields were low. Clusters and berries were small, and drought set a smaller-than-average crop.
claims.note: Search summaries put Cabernet 10 to 30% below normal at named estates. Not read directly.

claims.claim: Summer had no big heat spikes. June was mostly mid-80s F with one brief spike over 100, and late August and early September surges were short.
Harvest started very early. Whites came in from July 30 and reds from August 31, one of the earliest starts on record.
The harvest was cool and free of wildfire smoke. A late October storm came after the last grapes were in.
Reds have intense color and flavor, and Ehlers Estate reported lower alcohol this year.
Wine Independent calls the Cabernets a blend of 2018 and 2019: the brightness and structure of 2018 with the weight of 2019. The best may age 25 to 40 years or more.
claims.note: One critic's view, and the ageing figure is for the best wines only.

claims.claim: Search summaries say Decanter rated the vintage 5 out of 5 and Suckling called it very high quality in small quantity.

conflicts: Spring timing: Harvest Napa says early April budbreak. Wine Independent says Cabernet stayed dormant until mid-April. Vinography (summary only) says an early spring.
Harvest start: Harvest Napa says one of the earliest on record. No source read gives a reds-only range for Cabernet.

sheet.vintage: A dry, early year with a small crop. Small berries gave dark, concentrated reds. The harvest was cool and free of smoke.
